kind.description: Kind is program for a program hook; absent for an LLM hook (llm).

path.description:
Path is its file: its prompt, or its program's description file (in
the app's copy).

on.description: On is what it acts on: a watcher's events, of one type (or every type).

batch.description: Batch (an LLM hook's) gives one run every event that waited for it.

rate.description: Rate is how many runs it may start in any hour.

folder.description: Folder is where its runs work (absent: a temporary folder).

trusted.description:
Trusted is whether it may run for real (what it reaches and acts on
is what I trusted); Untrusted says why not.

turnOn.description:
TurnOn is true while turning it on (`hooks trust <hook> --yes
--resume`) has something to do: it's off, or it or its watcher isn't
trusted. Frontends offer Turn On… while it is.

problem.description:
Problem is why it can't run while it's on (its watcher missing,
untrusted or failing, ...); empty when it can.

servers.description:
Servers, Tools, BuiltinTools and Model are an LLM hook's, as an LLM
routine's: BuiltinTools are the agent CLI built-in tools its runs may use.

executable.description: Executable is the app's copy, the one that runs.

checksum.description: Checksum is the executable's SHA-256 (trust is keyed to it).

writes.description:
Writes is whether it can change anything: a dry run passes it
--dry-run; one that doesn't write runs as it is.

env.description: Env is the environment variable it's passed as.

items.description: ProgramSecret is a secret a program declares, and whether it's stored (`auth login <program>` stores it).

program.description: Program is a program hook's own: what runs and with what.

trigger.description:
Trigger is what started the run: "schedule", "manual", "backfill" or
(a hook's) "event" (empty in records from before triggers were
recorded).

for.description: For is the time the run is for (the schedule slot, the backfilled day).

id.description: ID is the run's history ID (as `runs show` takes).

sessionId.description:
SessionID is the run's saved agent CLI session (routines with
session: save): set when the run starts if the app picks its ID, when
it ends if the CLI does (Backend says which CLI resumes it).

backend.description:
Backend is the model backend running it, or that ran it (llm.backend's
value), once it got as far as the model.

folder.description:
Folder is the folder the run worked in (where its session resumes
from), unless it was an empty temporary one.

deadline.description: Deadline is when a running run is stopped (its routine's timeout).

queuedAt.description: QueuedAt is when the run started waiting for its turn, if it had to.

lastRun.description: LastRun is its latest outcome from run status.

label.description: Label is what the OS calls it (Input Monitoring).

state.description:
State is what the scheduler last found: granted, missing, unknown (it
can't be checked), unsupported (not on this OS) or not-checked
(nothing recorded yet). Only missing and not-checked keep it from
running.

items.description: PermissionSource is what declares a permission something needs: a plugin it uses, its own program (a program's, a program hook's) or its watcher.

where.description:
Where says where it's turned on, following "turn it on" ("in System
Settings > Privacy & Security > Input Monitoring"), and SettingsURL is
the address that opens it (absent where there's none).

items.description: PermissionNeed is a permission something needs, what declares it, and what the scheduler last found.

permissions.description:
Permissions are what the OS must allow it before it can work: its
action's (an LLM hook's plugins', a program hook's own) and its
watcher's, with what declares each and what the scheduler last found;
absent when none.

items.description: HookInfo is one row of `hooks list --json`: a hook with its effective settings and last run.
